name: Scroll container skips laying out kept content

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

hypothesisMarkdown:
## Scroll container skips laying out kept content

Mechanism: a scroll container whose layer is expected to composite (the layer holds composable content and the frame only scrolled it) does not request the layout of its children: it keeps the nodes, element states and dependencies its layer recorded when it last painted (`KeptContent`), and gives the children's layout back to them in prepaint if the layer is painted after all. Allowed: div.rs, fast/layers (reuse, policy, record, paint), fast/retained.rs recording wrappers, fast/layout.rs counters. Forbidden: list layers, views.
measurementPlanMarkdown: ab.sh over eight scenarios, 3 reps; a new test group (`fast::tests::layer_content_layout`); the oracle tests (frames through layers equal frames from scratch). Pass: scroll-div-cards draw down at least 20%, nothing else slower.
reportMarkdown:
## Scroll container skips laying out kept content Finished

Passed: true. On composited scroll frames the owner view still renders (user code) but the 400 cards' layout is not requested: no node claim per element, no style compare, no text measure; the nodes are kept by key. Two things had to hold for it to apply: the prediction needed the holding view while layout is requested (`invalidate::owner` knew it only in prepaint), and a repaint that was expected to composite must keep the layout for the next frames (the kept content is handed to the new record). New group `layer_content_layout` (2 tests, both fail without the skip); the 435 fast tests including the layer oracles and the 1,166 tests of the crate pass; clippy clean.

Attempt Count: 1.
decisionMarkdown:
### Decision

Committed success. What is left of a composited div-cards frame is the application's own render of 4,000 elements (memmove, Interactivity::new, drops).
